title: Collecting Mouse Livers for Transcriptome Analysis of Daily Rhythms
author: Mortimer, Welz, et al.
materials: RNA library prep kit for total RNA sequencing
dissection tools (forceps, small scissors, big scissors)

Timing: 2 days2.Extract RNA from the piece of liver in the 2 mL tube using an RNeasy plus mini kit (Qiagen), in accordance with the manufactureŕs instructions (https://www.qiagen.com/us/shop/automated-solutions/sequencers/rneasy-plus-mini-kit/)CRITICAL: Before proceeding to sequencing, validity of the collection should be checked by qPCR for clock genes (e.g., Bmal1, Dbp, Cry1, Per2, Rorc, Reverbα). High-amplitude rhythms with distinct phases should be apparent in wild-type mice (Figure 3; Table S1).

steps.title: Schedule liver collection
steps.instruction: Collect livers from one mouse at each of six Zeitgeber time points (ZT0, ZT4, ZT8, ZT12, ZT16, ZT20) over a 24‑hour cycle; adjust the light schedule as needed (e.g., Room 2 inverted: lights‑off 7:30 am, lights‑on 7:30 pm).

steps.title: Extract RNA from liver
steps.instruction: Place the dissected liver piece in a 2 mL tube and extract total RNA using the Qiagen RNeasy Plus Mini Kit, following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Validate RNA by qPCR
steps.instruction: Check the validity of each RNA sample by qPCR for clock genes (Bmal1, Dbp, Cry1, Per2, Rorc, Reverbα); high‑amplitude rhythms with distinct phases should be observed in wild‑type mice.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Prepare libraries with the Illumina TruSeq RNA v2 total‑RNA library preparation kit according to the kit instructions, then sequence each library to a depth of ~20 million single‑end reads (paired‑end or polyA‑enriched options are permissible).

steps.title: Process RNA‑seq data and QC
steps.instruction: Run a standard RNA‑seq pipeline (alignment, quantification) to obtain expression values (FPKM, RPKM, or TPM); perform quality‑control analyses such as Principal Component Analysis and hierarchical clustering to identify outlier samples.

steps.title: Install R and JTK_CYCLE scripts
steps.instruction: Download and install R from https://cran.r-project.org/, then download the JTK_CYCLE script package (JTKversion3.zip) from https://openwetware.org/wiki/File:JTKversion3.zip and unzip it into a dedicated directory.

steps.title: Create annotation file
steps.instruction: Make a tab‑delimited annotation file whose first column lists gene IDs (e.g., EntrezID) and subsequent columns contain desired annotations such as HUGO symbol and Ensembl ID.

steps.title: Create data matrix file
steps.instruction: Make a tab‑delimited data matrix file whose first column lists the same gene IDs, followed by columns for each time point (ZT0, ZT4, ZT8, …) with replicates placed adjacently (e.g., ZT0_1, ZT0_2, …).

steps.title: Save files as tab‑delimited
steps.instruction: Save both the annotation file and the data matrix file as .txt files in the same folder that contains the JTK_CYCLE scripts.

steps.title: Edit Run_JTK_CYCLE script
steps.instruction: Open Run_JTK_CYCLE (Example1).R in a text editor and modify the indicated lines to match your dataset.

substeps.instruction: Line 4: change the project name from the default "Example1" to a descriptive name.
Lines 7‑8: replace the default file names with your annotation and data matrix file names (e.g., "my_annot.txt" and "my_data.txt").
Line 12: set jtkdist(6,4) to reflect six time‑points and four replicates per point (adjust with group.size <- c(... ) and jtkdist(length(group.sizes),group.sizes) if replicate numbers differ).
Line 14: set periods <- 6:6 to restrict analysis to a 24‑hour period.
Line 15: set jtk.init(periods,4) because time‑points are spaced four hours apart.

steps.title: Set R working directory
steps.instruction: In an R session, set the working directory to the folder containing the scripts, annotation file, and data matrix file (e.g., setwd("/path/to/folder")).

steps.title: Run JTK_CYCLE analysis
steps.instruction: Source the edited Run_JTK_CYCLE (Example1).R script (paste it into the R console and press Enter); JTK_CYCLE will generate a tab‑delimited results file with BH.Q, ADJ.P, PER, LAG, and AMP for each gene (runtime ≈10‑15 min on a standard desktop).

steps.title: Filter rhythmic gene results
steps.instruction: Filter the output file to keep genes with an adjusted p‑value ≤ 0.01 (and optionally an amplitude threshold) to obtain a high‑confidence list of daily‑rhythmic transcripts.

steps.title: Downstream bioinformatics analyses
steps.instruction: Use the final list of rhythmic genes for downstream analyses such as gene‑ontology enrichment, pathway analysis, or to guide further in‑vivo/in‑vitro experiments.
